definition: Of, relating to, or characterized by rain; in geology, designating a period of greatly increased rainfall, especially one coinciding with a glacial epoch in higher latitudes.
etymology: From Latin pluvialis, rainy, which flows from pluvia, rain, itself from pluere, to rain. The Romans gave rain its own goddess, Pluvius Jupiter — the aspect of Jove invoked to bring or stop the downpour — and the word has been dripping through English since the seventeenth century.
usage: November presses down with a pluvial insistence today, the gutters running full and the garden paths turned to mirrors, as if the sky had decided the earth had not yet had enough.
